_read_me: The gate-duration anchor (#446). Nothing in tools/gate_clock.py writes this file, under any verb, ever: raising a value here is a deliberate hand-edit somebody makes on purpose, visible in the diff, because a number that moves by itself cannot detect slow growth. Lowering it after a measured improvement (#442, #447) is the same deliberate edit, and moves 'set' with it: each entry's 'set' bounds the report's window to green runs at or after it, so a lowered anchor never false-fires against the older, slower rows still in the records — instead the recipe reads insufficient_sample until five post-set green runs exist, which is the honest state of a re-set instrument. 'set' takes an ISO date (bounding from that day's start) or a full ISO timestamp (bounding from the moment it names — write the timestamp when re-setting on a day already run, or that morning's slower rows stay in the window). Every anchored entry needs a positive numeric 'anchor_seconds' and a 'set'; an entry carrying 'anchor_seconds': null names a recipe the recorder writes that no anchor has been derived for yet (#483 widened the recorded set past the two this file anchored) — the deliberate unset, read by the loader, and not the same as a dropped key, which is damage. The unset is readable only for a recipe no anchor was ever derived for: nulling 'anchor_seconds' on an anchored recipe is a disarmed instrument wearing a configuration choice's spelling, so the loader reads it as damage exactly like a dropped key and 'just check' reds. Which recipes are anchored is stated once, in ANCHORED_RECIPES in tools/gate_clock.py, and writing an anchor here for a new recipe adds it there in the same hand-edit — the file and that tuple cannot disagree without a red. The file names every recipe the recorder writes — the set RECIPES states in tools/gate_clock.py, never enumerated here — and a malformed file or entry, a recipe the file fails to name (deleted or misspelled), or a key the recorder does not write prints from 'report' and reddens 'just check' rather than reading as an unset anchor, which would be silence dressed as health. The threshold the anchor is compared against, and the measurement behind both, are tools/gate_clock.py's header.

check.note: Recorded since #483; no anchor derived yet. Deriving one is the deliberate hand-edit above, made from `just gate-clock-history` once enough green rows exist to take a median from.

mutation.note: Recorded since #483; no anchor derived yet. Its wall is diff-scoped where every other recipe's is not, so an anchor here would be read against `mutation_targets`, as fast's is.

unit.derivation: Re-set by #442/#452 (load never rebalances; the tier now runs --dist worksteal). Median of 10 green runs this day after the flag landed (71.3, 74.7, 71.2, 74.2, 71.8, 70.1, 69.4, 70.6, 69.4, 74.7 s), on the issue-442 worktree at 861eb6a plus the change, uncommitted. 1-minute load before each run 0.25 to 5.49, and foreign_gate_processes 0 on every row, read from the gate-clock records themselves (#446's durable instrument) rather than from in-session observation — load context is what distinguishes a scheduler gain from a quieter-box gain, so it rests on the record. 5155 Python tests collected, 17 Rust. The pre-change arm the same morning, same box and clock: 158.8, 148.2, 150.7, 150.2 s (median 150.45). The set moment is a timestamp, not a date, so this morning's slower load-scheduler rows stay out of the window.

fast.derivation: Re-set for #660 from the current durable gate-clock records, re-measured after #644 rather than inheriting its 12a40052 snapshot. I chose the recent all-condition population because the fast anchor should represent ordinary gate operation; load strata are reported as sensitivity checks, not used to bias the baseline. Selection: 86 green fast rows at or after 2026-08-27T00:00:00+00:00 with mutation_targets > 0, using the recorder's had_mutation_target filter. Their median wall is 163.08 s (middle walls 160.82 and 165.33 s); load_1m median is 3.69, range 111.13 to 296.66 s. The quiet-box check, load_1m < 3, has 38 rows and a 145.78 s median (middle walls 145.61 and 145.95 s); the loaded check, load_1m >= 5, has 35 rows and a 186.41 s median. With THRESHOLD=1.25, the new fire point is 203.85 s: exactly 1.25x the all-condition median and 1.40x the quiet-box median. #446's documented 232 s regression endpoint remains above it at 1.42x the all-condition median and 1.59x the quiet-box median, so this hand-edit restores sensitivity while retaining the threshold. The full ISO set timestamp excludes all older rows; the post-set report therefore remains insufficient_sample until five comparable green rows exist.
